sentences.text:
Rajaram Bhadu vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45684) on 12
November, 2024
Author: Farjand Ali
Bench: Farjand Ali

[2024:Rj-Jd:45684]
 High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At

Jodhpur
 S.B. Criminal Misc(Pet.) No. 7826/2024
Rajaram Bhadu S/o Sh. Laluram Bhadu, Aged About 39 Years, R/
o Mankasar, Teh.

And Ps Bajju, Dist. Bikaner, Raj.
 ----Petitioner
 Versus
1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp
2.

Edrish Khan S/o Ali Khan, R/o Bhanavatawala, Ps Pugal,
 Dist. Bikaner Presently R/o 670-800 R.d., Ps Pugal, Dist.
 Bikaner, Raj.
 ----Respondents

For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Dev Krishna Gaur For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vikram Rajpurohit, Dy.G.A.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Order 12/11/2024 1.

The instant criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner for quashing of FIR No.121 registered at Police Station Pugal, District Bikaner for the offence under Sections 420, 406 IPC.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner prays for quashing the aforementioned FIR and all further proceeding in pursuant thereof.

3. Per contra, learned Dy.G.A. opposes the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner for quashing of the FIR as well as all further proceeding in pursuant thereof and submits a factual report dated 07.11.2024 sent by office of SHO, Police Station Pugal, District Bikaner wherein after investigation in the present case, a charge-sheet has been chalked out and the same has been submitted before the M.J.M. Court, Khajuwala, District Bikaner.

entities.text: Rajaram Bhadu vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45684)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Be that as it may, since the investigation has been completed, the charge-sheet has already been filed before the learned trial court and the offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 420 & 406 IPC, which does not contain sentence of more than seven years, for which the provision contained under Sections 41 & 41A Cr.P.C. are applies mutatis mutandis so also the judgment passed by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kuamr Vs. State of Bihar : AIR 2014 SC 2756 applies squarely in the present case, therefore, instead of going into the niceties of the matter,
it is deemed appropriate to direct the petitioner to appear before the learned trial Court on or before 10.12.2024 and to move a regular bail application under Section 437 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Arnesh Kuamr Vs. State of Bihar : AIR 2014 SC 2756
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Upon doing so, the learned trial court shall release him on bail on the very same day on the amount of surety and bonds as it deems fit.
4. The petitioner would be at liberty to raise all his grounds before the learned trial court as raised here in this petition.
5. Accordingly, the criminal misc. petition as well as stay petition are disposed of.
6. Factual report be taken on record.

(FARJAND ALI),J 77-chhavi/-
